title: Academia is for Ambition — Alex Zhang, MIT
subtitle: We catch up with RLM first author Alex Zhang, MIT PhD, on Jev, PhD masxing, and the future of harnesses.

While we tend to cover industry on the pod, every so often we celebrate a clearly emerging superstar PhD. In 2024 we featured Shunyu Yao , who went on to build Operator at OpenAI and is now Chief AI Scientist of Tencent . In 2025 we featured Jack Morris , who went on to cofound Engram at $600m and is now a leading voice on continual learning .
This year we are proud to feature the work of Alex Zhang of MIT.

From GPU kernels and KernelBench to Recursive Language Models , Mismanaged Geniuses , and massive multi-agent swarms, Alex Zhang is exploring how much capability we’re leaving on the table by wrapping increasingly powerful models in primitive systems.
RLMs took over the timeline early this year:
and an RLM based harness was the first to ~solve ARC-AGI-3 before OpenAI’s Astra:
and is even today, influencing new research that has more extreme implications than RLMs:

We go deep on GPU Mode and AI-written kernels, research taste and why academics should take bets industry labs won’t, GEV and alternatives to the standard autoregressive language model, and the idea of harnesses as compositional generalizers. Alex explains RLMs, context offloading, programmatic subagent calling, Prime Agent, persistent subagents, and why the “language model” of the future may actually be an invisible swarm of agents underneath a simple interface. We also discuss OpenAI’s massive agent experiments, Kimi swarms, open-ended research at Sakana AI, speculative programmatic tool calling, capability overhang, Neuralese, and where Alex thinks the next big research opportunities may lie.

summary.one_liner: MIT 的 Alex Zhang 剖析 RLM、Harness 架構與 Agent Swarm，主張透過程式碼與上下文卸載打破傳統 LLM 限制。

topics.title: GPU 核心優化與人類專家價值
topics.body: 雖然 GPU Mode 排行榜上很多解答都是 AI 生成的，但人類專家的直覺依然是巨大優勢。例如成員 Gauners 寫出的核心是前十名中唯一在端到端系統中真正穩定的。AI 容易陷入 reward hacking，而專家知道如何給予正確的引導與驗證，一項專家的關鍵洞見就能省下幾千億甚至一兆個 token 的暴力搜尋。

topics.title: 突破自迴歸框架與 GEV 概念
topics.body: 大眾已習慣把語言模型等同於自迴歸 Transformer 解碼器，但像 GEV 這類嘗試展示了改變輸出空間的可能性。若任務只是二元分類，透過改變輸出結構能大幅降低推論延遲與成本，不必每次都呼叫龐大的 text-to-text 模型。這種在模型內透過不同輸出空間或路由來換取延遲與運算效率的思路，是 RLM 等複雜系統亟需的。

topics.title: Harness 是組合泛化器與 RLM 本質
topics.body: 現有許多 Harness 其實結構非常雷同，多數採用將整個軌跡當成 Prompt 的單一迴圈。RLM（遞迴語言模型）的核心設計則是將上下文卸載到外部記憶體（如檔案系統或 REPL），並將程式碼執行視為唯一工具，讓模型透過程式化遞迴呼叫子代理。透過這種設計，高層的解題策略在檢索或聚合等不同任務上呈現一致性，讓模型在短任務上訓練後能直接泛化到長度長 8 到 30 倍的任務。

topics.title: Prime Agent 與持久化子代理
topics.body: Prime Agent 是基於 Pi Mono 建構的 RLM Harness，將 IPython 設為唯一工具，其餘工具皆以 Python 模組或 Bash 腳本載入。它整合了 Continual Harness 概念，讓代理能動態修改自身技能、系統提示詞與可用子代理。此外，Prime Agent 透過檔案系統實現持久化子代理，允許子代理在主任務結束後繼續存在，讓工程師能後續追問並保有更高可觀測性。

topics.title: Agent Swarm 的收斂挑戰與未來模型型態
topics.body: OpenAI 在解決 Navier–Stokes 問題時動用了 1 萬個代理、耗費 1300 億輸出 token，但本質上是一群具備共享檔案系統的代理群在做深度搜尋。目前的 Swarm 往往有 95% 的計算是在浪費 token，如何讓 Swarm 穩定收斂至解答是極高門檻。未來使用者 query 的「單一語言模型」，底層可能其實是一整套看不見的 Swarm 或大型 Harness 脚手架。

topics.title: 投機性工具呼叫與能力懸垂
topics.body: 針對程式化工具呼叫，推動 Speculative Tool Calling 能在模型產生程式碼的過程中，透過靜態分析提前觸發相依工具，消除序列等待。現有前端模型在撰寫程式和數學上極強，但缺乏將這些能力轉移到長期穩定任務的 Harness。目前存在明顯的能力懸垂（Capability Overhang），就算底層模型不升級，光靠設計出能勝任長期、穩定簡單工作的 Harness，就能解鎖龐大產值。

insights.title: 將上下文卸載至檔案系統以維持局部分佈內
insights.body: 避免將所有多輪對話歷史無腦塞進 Context Window；將軌跡外部化為檔案或 REPL 狀態，讓每個子代理只接收聚焦的局部問題，確保每次 LLM 呼叫都在分佈內（In-Distribution）。

insights.title: 將程式碼執行作為 Agent 溝通與工具調用的唯一界面
insights.body: 捨棄脆弱的單步 JSON Tool Calling，改以 Python/IPython 環境為中心，讓 Agent 透過編寫程式碼來調度工具、遞迴呼叫子代理並傳遞共享記憶體，大幅提升解題邏輯的組合性與彈性。

insights.title: 善用持久化子代理提升長工作流的可維護性
insights.body: 在架構中打破子代理呼叫完即拋棄的限制，將其狀態持久化儲存，使工程師或主代理能隨時介入重啟上下文，解決長任務除錯與狀態丟失的痛點。

quotes.speaker: Alex Zhang
quotes.en: I think the thing that we’ve kind of discovered with all these agent swarms and things like this is, like, when you throw enough compute at a problem, you, like, can sufficiently explore solutions to that problem. But oftentimes, like, maybe you can burn, like, 100 billion or a trillion tokens on something, but if you bring in someone who knows something about the problem, they can uncover something for the model that would, like, erase that one trillion token spend.
quotes.zh: 我認為我們在這些 Agent Swarm 中發現的是，當你投入足夠算力時，確實能充分探索解法。但很多時候，你可能會燒掉一千億或一兆個 token，而如果你找來一個真正懂該領域的人，他為模型點出關鍵，就能省下那一兆 token 的消耗。

quotes.speaker: Alex Zhang
quotes.en: An RLM is basically just a harness design where the only tool in the harness is code, which is this programmatic subagent calling thing, where it has the option to call itself as a tool, and it has other tools. But all of these things are functions in code, and the context that it’s dealing with is always stored in some memory inside of this code environment.
quotes.zh: RLM 基本上就是一種 Harness 設計，其中唯一的工具就是程式碼——也就是這種以程式化呼叫子代理的機制，它能把呼叫自己當成工具，也包含其他工具。但所有這些東西都是程式碼裡的函式，而它處理的上下文永遠儲存在這個程式碼環境的某個記憶體中。

quotes.speaker: Alex Zhang
quotes.en: I think we will start to see in the future probably one day, and I wrote a blog about this, what we think of as a language model, like the thing that we query, might actually be like a swarm or like a scaffold or like some Weird harness design that scales very well, but the user just doesn’t see it.
quotes.zh: 我認為未來有一天我們會看到，我們所認知的語言模型（也就是我們 query 的那個物件），背後可能其實是一個 Swarm、一個 Scaffold，或是某種能高度擴展的奇特 Harness 設計，只是使用者完全看不到它。

quotes.speaker: Alex Zhang
quotes.en: I’m. Fairly certain that, like, 95% of the swarm is entirely useless, or, like, what it’s exploring is entirely u-- You’re just burning tokens.
quotes.zh: 我相當肯定 Swarm 中有 95% 基本上是完全無用的，或者說它探索的方向完全無用——你只是在純粹燒 token。

guests.intro: MIT 博士生、RLM（Recursive Language Models）論文第一作者，曾活躍於 GPU Mode 社群並推動 KernelBench，專注於 Agent Harness 架構與模型泛化研究。

summary.one_liner: Alex Zhang from MIT dissects RLMs, Harness architectures, and Agent Swarms, arguing for breaking traditional LLM limitations through code and context offloading.

topics.title: GPU Kernel Optimization and the Value of Human Experts
topics.body: Although many solutions on the GPU Mode leaderboard are AI-generated, human expert intuition remains a massive advantage. For example, the kernel written by member Gauners was the only one in the top ten that proved truly stable in an end-to-end system. AI is prone to reward hacking, whereas experts know how to provide the right guidance and verification—a single key insight from an expert can save hundreds of billions or even a trillion tokens of brute-force search.

topics.title: Breaking the Autoregressive Paradigm and the GEV Concept
topics.body: The public has grown accustomed to equating language models with autoregressive Transformer decoders, but efforts like GEV demonstrate the potential of altering the output space. If a task is merely binary classification, altering the output structure can drastically cut inference latency and cost without needing to invoke a massive text-to-text model every time. This mindset of trading latency and computational efficiency via alternative output spaces or routing inside the model is urgently needed for complex systems like RLMs.

topics.title: Harnesses as Compositional Generalizers and the Essence of RLMs
topics.body: Many existing harnesses actually share very similar structures, mostly relying on a single loop that treats the entire trajectory as the prompt. The core design of RLMs (Recursive Language Models) offloads context to external memory (such as a filesystem or REPL) and treats code execution as the sole tool, enabling the model to programmatically call sub-agents recursively. Through this design, high-level problem-solving strategies remain consistent across diverse tasks like retrieval or aggregation, allowing models trained on short tasks to generalize directly to tasks 8 to 30 times longer.

topics.title: Prime Agent and Persistent Sub-agents
topics.body: Prime Agent is an RLM Harness built on Pi Mono that sets IPython as the only tool, loading all other tools as Python modules or Bash scripts. It integrates the Continual Harness concept, allowing agents to dynamically modify their own skills, system prompts, and available sub-agents. Furthermore, Prime Agent implements persistent sub-agents via the filesystem, enabling them to persist after the main task finishes so engineers can follow up with queries and maintain higher observability.

topics.title: Convergence Challenges of Agent Swarms and Future Model Formats
topics.body: When tackling the Navier–Stokes problem, OpenAI deployed 10,000 agents and consumed 130 billion output tokens, but fundamentally it was a swarm of agents sharing a filesystem conducting deep search. Currently, around 95% of a swarm's compute is often wasted on tokens; getting a swarm to converge stably to a solution presents an extremely high bar. In the future, the "single language model" a user queries might actually be an entire invisible swarm or massive harness scaffolding underneath.

topics.title: Speculative Tool Calling and Capability Overhang
topics.body: For programmatic tool calling, advancing Speculative Tool Calling can trigger dependent tools ahead of time via static analysis while the model is still generating code, eliminating sequential wait times. Frontier models today are exceptionally strong at coding and mathematics, but they lack harnesses that transfer these capabilities into long-horizon, stable tasks. A clear capability overhang exists right now—even without upgrading underlying models, simply designing harnesses capable of reliable, long-horizon, straightforward work could unlock massive economic value.

insights.title: Offload Context to the Filesystem to Keep Calls In-Distribution
insights.body: Avoid mindlessly stuffing all multi-turn dialogue history into the context window; externalize trajectories into files or REPL states so each sub-agent receives only a focused, local problem, ensuring every LLM invocation remains in-distribution.

insights.title: Use Code Execution as the Sole Interface for Agent Communication and Tool Calling
insights.body: Abandon brittle single-step JSON tool calling in favor of a Python/IPython-centric environment, empowering agents to orchestrate tools, recursively invoke sub-agents, and pass shared memory via code, dramatically boosting the compositionality and flexibility of problem-solving logic.

insights.title: Leverage Persistent Sub-agents to Improve Long-Workflow Maintainability
insights.body: Break away from the limitation of disposable, fire-and-forget sub-agents by persisting their state within the architecture. This allows engineers or main agents to step in and resume context at any time, resolving the pain points of debugging long-running tasks and state loss.
